steps.observation: You have 10 seconds. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
A transformer turns each token into a vector (plus a positional embedding), then passes them through stacked layers of:  
1) Multi‐head self‐attention – each token computes “queries,” “keys,” and “values” to weigh and mix information from every other token in parallel,  
2) A small feed-forward network,  
with residual connections and layer-norm around each block.  
In encoder–decoder models, the decoder adds masked self‐attention (to prevent peeking ahead) and cross‐attention to the encoder’s outputs.  
This lets the model build deep, context-aware representations and generate sequences efficiently.
